blurb: Nonprofits and open source foundations stewarding models, standards, and shared infrastructure, with governance model and funding.

reading.body:
Four organizations appear here: two nonprofits and two open-source foundations with roles that touch AI tooling and evaluation, but none of them are infrastructure builders in the compute-or-power sense.

LMSYS is the most directly AI-central entry. It stewards Chatbot Arena, a shared evaluation platform that the broader AI community uses to benchmark model quality. That kind of neutral, open evaluation infrastructure matters because model comparison depends on it, yet it sits outside the commercial incentives of the labs being evaluated. Khan Academy is an end-user of AI capability in education, not a producer of it. The Krita Foundation and Blender Foundation steward creative software tools that AI-generated imagery and 3D content increasingly intersect with, but their primary missions predate and are not defined by AI.

What this data does not cover is significant. There are no training compute providers, no standards bodies setting grid or data-center specifications, and no open-model foundations of the kind that release weights for public use. The list is small, four entries, and the notes confirm only organizational structure and nonprofit status, not funding scale, compute access, or governance detail. A reader wanting to understand how nonprofit structures shape AI development at the infrastructure level will not find that answer here.
